issues.legal_issue: An application for substitution filed by either party that identifies the deceased party’s legal representatives is sufficient, and the opposing party is not required to file a separate substitution application.
A prayer for substitution may be construed as an implied prayer to set aside abatement, even without a separate express application for that relief.

Under Order XXII Rule 10-A of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court must clearly and unambiguously notify the opposing party of a respondent’s death, including the date of death, unless that party has already been effectively notified.

An appeal should not be treated as abated where the opposing party was not duly notified of the respondent’s death and the delay in seeking substitution therefore cannot fairly be attributed to the appellant.
